name: Cambodia
summary: Independent from France in 1953; the Khmer Rouge (1975–79) killed about 1.5–2 million people; a kingdom again since 1993.

terrain.value: A low-lying central plain around the Tonlé Sap and the Mekong.

climate.value: Tropical monsoon, with a wet season from May to October and a dry season.

urbanisation.value: Phnom Penh is the capital and largest city.

disease.value: Health care has improved since the 1990s, though malaria and dengue persist.

migration.value: Cities emptied by the Khmer Rouge (1975).

economicBase.value: Agriculture is the dominant sector; garments and tourism are growing.

tradeRoutes.value: The Mekong River and the Tonlé Sap lake carry traffic, and the port of Sihanoukville is growing.

wealth.value: The UN classes Cambodia as a least developed country.

moneyAndTax.value: The riel is official; the US dollar is used de facto.

governmentType.value: A constitutional monarchy in which the CPP dominates as a de facto one-party state.

keyRulers.value: Norodom Sihanouk (king; independence in 1953). Pol Pot (Khmer Rouge leader). Later and present leaders are not named here.

succession.value: In 2018 the CPP won every National Assembly seat without major opposition; the main opposition was disqualified in 2023.

stability.value: Khmer Rouge rule (1975–79), which committed genocide.

eliteConflict.value: Competition between political parties and leaders.

armyAndTech.value: The Royal Cambodian Armed Forces, which grew out of the former rival factions.

majorWars.value: Civil war (1970–75), ended by the Khmer Republic's surrender in April 1975; Vietnamese invasion (November 1978).

territoryChange.value: The borders have remained largely unchanged since independence, though disputes with Thailand and Vietnam occur.

alliancesRivals.value: Close ties with China, including investment and diplomatic support.

inventions.value: No major inventions are associated with the modern state.

scienceEducation.value: Schools and universities were rebuilt after 1979, when the Khmer Rouge had destroyed much of the educated class.

openness.value: Open to trade and foreign investment, with periods of restriction.

communicationTransport.value: Rivers, roads and a railway link Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville.

religion.value: Theravada Buddhism is the official religion, practised by over 95% of the population.

languageWriting.value: Khmer (about 95% of the population), written in the Khmer script, which is official.

artsArchitecture.value: Angkor Wat and Khmer classical dance.

socialStructure.value: A Khmer majority, with Cham, Vietnamese and Chinese minorities.

sharedIdentity.value: Pride in the Angkor heritage and Khmer culture holds the country together.

dailyLife.value: Many families live in houses on stilts and eat rice and fish, with prahok (fermented fish) common.

neighbours.value: Thailand, Laos and Vietnam, with the Gulf of Thailand to the south-west.

ideasReligions.value: Theravada Buddhism is the state religion.

colonisation.value: A French protectorate from 11 August 1863 until independence on 9 November 1953.

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
